question.problem:
The matrix $W$ is given below. Let ${w}_{1}$, ${w}_{2}$, and ${w}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $W.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{w}_{1},{w}_{3}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(W).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${w}_{2}={x}_{1}{w}_{1}+{x}_{3}{w}_{3}.$

$$
W=[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 10\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $W$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -9 & 6 \\ -5 & 15 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -5 & 15 & 10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{20}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(W)$ is $\{{w}_{1},{w}_{3}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $2$nd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${w}_{2}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 15\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{2}}={{(-3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{1}}+{{(0)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{w}_{3}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{3}=(-3)\cdot 0=0.$
